majors.what: `cloneCommand`'s *depth* is unpinned. Replacing `structuredClone(command)` with a shallow `{ ...command }` leaves all 243 tests green (verified: full suite, 10 files, 227 in the document dir plus the rest). The only test guarding this mechanism — history.test.ts:161 'replays the command it recorded, not the object the caller kept' — uses `slide.setHtml`, whose entire payload is a string, and a spread protects strings just as well as a deep clone. Under the shallow mutant I reproduced r1's major #1 end-to-end through the redo path: apply `{t:'slide.insert', slide: entry, ...}`, `undo()`, then `entry.title = 'HIJACKED-VIA-REDO'`, then `redo()` — the document comes back titled `HIJACKED-VIA-REDO` (deep clone: `Original`). The same hole exists for `deck.setTheme`'s `theme` object.
majors.why: This is the identical shape of finding r1 raised for `unshift`→`push` and the builder accepted: the mechanism is correct today, and one word of 'simplification' silently reverts it with the suite green. It is more than theoretical here because the change gives someone an active reason to make that edit — I measured `apply` of a 2 MB `slide.setHtml` at 2.76 ms per call (20 iterations), essentially all of it the `structuredClone` of a string that is immutable and needs no deep copy. The next person profiling the design-mode edit path will reach for the spread, and nothing will stop them. The commit message's claim 'Three tests, each red under its mutant' is true for the mutant chosen (`[...commands]`) but not for the depth the fix actually relies on.
majors.fix: Add one assertion to the existing history test using a nested payload — apply a `slide.insert`, `undo()`, mutate `command.slide.title`, `redo()`, assert the restored entry's title. Two lines, and it makes the shallow-copy mutant red. (If the 2.76 ms/2 MB cost later matters, the honest optimization is a per-variant copy — spread for the string-only variants, `structuredClone` for `slide.insert`/`deck.setTheme`/`deck.setThemeTokens`/`deck.setMeta` — which that test would then be protecting.)

minors.what: Nit: `structuredClone` moved a throw inside `applyCommand`, which line 493 documents as 'Never throws, never mutates'. Verified: a `SlideEntry` carrying a function-valued extra key makes `applyCommand` throw a `DOMException` (DataCloneError) instead of returning `{ ok: false, code: 'invalid-slide-entry' }`. TypeScript's excess-property check does not stop this when the entry is bound to a variable before being placed in the command.
minors.why: No producer can reach it today — every command source (IPC payload, agent tool call, `.sloodge` bytes) is JSON and therefore clonable — and the throw is loud and happens before any state changes, so it cannot corrupt a document. It is worth a line only because 'errors are values, never throws' (line 17) is an explicit convention of this layer and a `DOMException` escaping `history.apply` into an IPC handler would arrive with no error code. Note the clone-then-validate order is *right* and should stay: validating the caller's object and then cloning it would be a TOCTOU gap against a getter.
minors.fix: Wrap the clone in `try/catch` and return `err('invalid-slide-entry', 'entry is not structured-cloneable')`; same for the theme at line 401. Or narrow the docblock claim at line 493.

minors.what: Nit: the new `JSON.stringify(command.slide).length` term — the whole of the minor-4 fix — is unpinned. Replacing it with `0` leaves the suite green. The byte-cap eviction tests exist but none depends on a `slide.insert`'s entry being counted.
minors.why: Low stakes by construction: `commandBytes` is documented as an estimate feeding a soft cap, and I confirmed the new number is now conservative in the safe direction (a `slide.remove` entry reports 624 bytes against 487 bytes of real serialized payload, where r1 measured 301 against 487). Pinning an estimate's exact value would be over-specification; pinning its *shape* would not.
minors.fix: Optional. One assertion that `commandBytes` of a `slide.insert` exceeds `html.length + 128`, or leave it — the docblock is now honest about what the number is.

minors.what: Nit: `invertGroup`'s null-prototype comment claims 'the inverse of a `__proto__` token has to be a real key too, or it would report success while restoring nothing', but that consequence cannot occur. `applyBatch` inverts before it applies, and the forward `deck.setThemeTokens` carrying a `__proto__` token is now rejected by `parseTheme`, so the whole batch aborts and the inverse is never stacked. Correspondingly the mutant survives: changing `emptyMap<V | null>()` back to `{}` leaves all 243 tests green (unlike the `mergeGroup` half, which is correctly pinned by the new test at commands.test.ts:517).
minors.why: The change itself is right — uniform null-prototype maps are the file's stated discipline and cost nothing. Only the justification has drifted: it asserts an observable failure that the sibling fix in `mergeGroup` has already made unreachable, which is the kind of comment a future reader trusts and then wastes an hour trying to reproduce.
minors.fix: Reword to 'for uniformity with `mergeGroup` and the rest of this file's maps; unobservable today because the forward patch is rejected first.'

verification.lint: pnpm exec oxlint src tests — exit 0 (no diagnostics); pnpm exec prettier --check src tests — exit 0, all files formatted
verification.test: pnpm test (vitest run) — exit 0, 10 files, 243 passed, matching the fix commit's claim of 237 -> 243
verification.worktree: git status --porcelain clean before and after. All mutants applied via perl in-place and restored from backups in the scratchpad; both scratch probe files deleted; final full run re-verified green after restoration.

r1_findings_reverified.major_1_aliasing: FIXED, and verified with r1's own probes plus a stronger one. `doc.manifest.slides[entry.id] === entry` is now `false`; `entry.title = 'HIJACKED'` after apply leaves the document reading 'Original'; mutating `cmd.html` after apply no longer changes what `redo()` replays. I then ran an exhaustive reference-graph scan — for all 8 command variants, every object reachable from the command was checked against every object reachable from the resulting document, and there were zero shared references. The boundary cannot be bypassed: the clones live inside `applyCommand`, so `applyBatch`, `history.apply` and a transaction all inherit them (verified all three). Reverting either `structuredClone` reds its own new test. The caveat is the depth of `cloneCommand`, raised as the major above.
r1_findings_reverified.major_2_transaction_order: FIXED and correctly pinned. `open.inverse.unshift` -> `push` now reds exactly one test — history.test.ts:295 'undoes non-commuting batches in reverse order, exactly' — and nothing else. The test asserts both the recorded `entry.inverse` command-type order (move, move, insert) and exact document restoration, which is the pair r1 asked for.
r1_findings_reverified.minor_1_dead_guard: FIXED. The `entry.file` guard and its drifted comment are gone; `slideFilePath` is no longer imported (lint would have caught a stale import, and did not fire).
r1_findings_reverified.minor_2_proto_maps: FIXED for `mergeGroup` (mutant reds the new computed-key `__proto__` test), unpinned and slightly over-claimed for `invertGroup` — minor 3 above.
r1_findings_reverified.minor_3_untested_defensive_branches: FIXED for the reachable one: reordering `undo()` to pop before checking `applied.ok` now reds 'does not touch the document or the stacks when an undo cannot be applied'. I independently verified the `abortTransaction` sibling really is unreachable rather than merely inconvenient — every command in `open.inverse` was inverted against the exact state its forward command was applied to, `#push` never runs while a transaction is open, and `reset()`/`commit` are the only other exits — including the tricky insert-then-remove-the-same-slide case, which rolls back cleanly. Documenting it instead of pinning it is the right call.
r1_findings_reverified.minor_4_byte_accounting: FIXED in direction and honesty; unpinned — minor 2 above.

hypotheses_tested: The clone boundary leaves some *other* variant aliasing caller memory. REJECTED by exhaustive reference-graph diff over all 8 variants: `slide.setHtml`/`slide.setNotes` carry only immutable strings; `deck.setThemeTokens` copies each group through `copyMap` (primitive values only) and `series` through a spread; `deck.setMeta` spreads `authors`. Zero shared references in any case.

The clone points can be bypassed through `applyBatch` or a transaction. REJECTED — both route through `applyCommand`; a `slide.insert` applied inside `beginTransaction`/`commitTransaction` and one applied through `applyBatch` directly both survive a post-hoc `entry.title = 'HIJACKED'` untouched.

`cloneCommand`'s depth is unpinned and a shallow copy reintroduces r1's major. CONFIRMED — full suite green under `{ ...command }`, and `redo()` then replays a caller-mutated `slide.insert` entry into the live document. Raised as the major.

`history.apply` clones `forward` but *not* `applied.inverse`, so the undo stack aliases document objects. CONFIRMED as real aliasing but REJECTED as a defect: `undoStack()[0].inverse[0].theme === doc.theme` and a removed slide's inverse carries the live manifest entry by reference — but both are document-owned values, and documents in this layer are immutable by construction (r1 verified nothing writes in place, against a recursively frozen doc). After an undo the restored document holds a fresh clone, not the stacked object, so the two never converge. The remaining door — `new DocumentHistory(doc)` and `reset(doc)` take the caller's document by reference — is an explicit ownership transfer stated at history.ts:4 and is the same shape store.ts already has.
`structuredClone` introduces a throw into a layer that promises error values. CONFIRMED as a contract gap but unreachable by any real producer. Raised as minor 1.

The deep clone is a per-edit performance regression. CONFIRMED as measurable, judged acceptable: 2.76 ms per `apply` of a 2 MB `slide.setHtml` (mean of 20), essentially all of it copying an immutable string. Design-mode's 500 ms coalescing (40-design-mode.md) is deferred but is the consumer that would care, so the cost lands at ~2 applies/second. Folded into the major's rationale because it is what makes the shallow-copy refactor tempting.

The `notes: undefined` normalization in `applySlideSetNotes` is only pinned by `toStrictEqual`, and every round-trip assertion in these tests uses `toEqual` (which ignores undefined-valued keys). REJECTED — replacing the entry rebuild with `{ ...entry, notes: undefined }` reds 'removes both the text and the manifest reference, and round-trips'. The tests assert the key's absence directly, not only through deep equality.

Byte accounting is now wrong for inverse batches. REJECTED — a delete's inverse (`slide.insert` carrying the entry and the HTML) is the case r1 flagged and it is now the case that is counted; the estimate errs high (624 reported vs 487 serialized) rather than low, which is the safe direction for a cap.
`commandBytes`'s new entry term is unpinned. CONFIRMED (mutant to `0` survives). Raised as minor 2.
`invertGroup`'s null-prototype change is unpinned and its comment over-claims. CONFIRMED. Raised as minor 3.
`abortTransaction`'s failure branch is reachable after all. REJECTED — see minor_3 above; I could not construct a sequence reaching it without writing to the private open transaction.
not_reviewed: r1's 14 falsified hypotheses (round-trip totality, serializability, precondition completeness, prototype keys on slide-id commands, generic/extras preservation, eviction behaviour, redo byte staleness, exhaustiveness under a 9th variant) were not re-litigated; nothing in commit 87fe15e touches those paths.

`git diff main` also shows the `fix-open-external` work (src/main/security/externalUrls.ts, src/main/index.ts, its tests and reviews) as deleted, because this branch forked before main landed it. Out of scope for M1.2 and not reviewed; it will disappear on rebase.
notes.summary: The fix commit is honest and lands every r1 finding: the copy boundary is real and I could not find a single caller-owned object reaching the document through any of the 8 command variants, `applyBatch`, or a transaction; the transaction inverse order is now pinned by a non-commuting test that is the sole red under the `unshift`->`push` mutant; the dead guard is gone; the null-prototype maps are right; and the byte cap's limits are documented rather than papered over. One thing to close before merge, and it is the mirror of the finding r1 opened with: the *depth* of `cloneCommand` — the half of the fix that protects the redo stack — is not pinned by any test, so a shallow spread passes all 243 tests while letting a caller's post-apply edit to a `slide.insert` entry reappear in the document on redo. Two lines of test.
